text.text_excerpt: I frequently jog past Who Dat Cafe and had been wanting to try Milkfish, which is inside. I FINALLY got the chance last weekend while trying to get away from all of the post jazz fest crowds in the Quarter and holy cow was it good. I have been missing some hard core Filipino food since moving away from the Bay Area and this place really hit the spot. My husband is not an adventurous eater so he ordered the spam fried rice with the egg on top and chicken adobo. The rice was wonderful, especially seeing as though it was my first time eating spam (spam is MY idea of adventurous food). Although my guy thought the chicken could have used a bit more flavor, he still thinks it is some of the bes...

Today my friend Karen and I made a trip over to the Bywater for some Filipino food. We started off with the appetizer plate which was 5 lumpia shanghai rolls and 2 large lumpia rolls as well as 2 longanisa sausages for $14. Everything was great. The lumpia is just like my mom's and the Longanisa was good although I would have liked some vinegar served with it. It was also a little more expensive than I was expecting, all that being said, it was still very good and just like Mom's We then had spam rice which was basically pan fried small chunks of spam mixed with fried rice, green onions, fresh tomatoes and topped with a fried egg for $8. It was DELICIOUS and the pricing was spot on. I kno...

GREAT Filipino place in the back of Who Dat Cafe. Food was delicious; can't wait to try more of the adventurous items. We had the appetizer sampler (chicken skewers and lumpia eggrolls were the best) and the chicken pancit (the glass noodles are top notch). Waitress was very nice and knowledgable. Plus, she crafted the entire cocktail list herself. Great, inexpensive place for a mid-week meal. Plus, the portions were HUGE. Look forward to trying more of the food.
